name: mirage
text:
Not proven yet. Nothing has a profit interval that clearly stays above zero with a good sample.
What I can say, ranked by how much I trust it:
1. Bids on team totals, the best candidate. Earlier study: about 65 filled bids, +34% ROI, and they beat the closing line by about 2.4% (t=4.4). The closing-line result is strong, but 65 bets is too few to trust the profit.
2. Player props, in the engine's own orders: about +25% on 137 settled bets. The closing line backs it up, but the sample is small and the old by-hand prop overs lost money.
3. NBA: +6.8% on 620 bets. That's a decent sample, but the margin of error at that size is about ±8 points, so it isn't proven.
4. NFL: +7.0% on only 78 bets, so too few.
Proven losers: NCAAB -5.1% on 1,570 bets, game totals -8.1% on 1,094, and by-hand prop overs (-15%).
Across all 17,674 bets the app has logged, the average edge against the closing line is about +0.04%. That means the scanner finds fair-priced bets, not clearly +EV ones, so no feed has been shown to pay for itself yet.
Next I'll read NCAAB's closing-line results, then limit the engine to the types that beat the close (NBA, props, team-total bids). Re-test after about 300 more settled bets in each type.
